messages.subject: target-runner vs instances
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I was successful on adapting my exe code to directly parse the arguments coming from iRace, and its working well on windows without using the bat file.
My question is: What is then Instances folder and the  "instances-list.txt" list for? I did not quite got the difference or application. And I can't leave the Instances folder empty.

Thanks in advance.

messages.subject: Re: target-runner vs instances
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ignacio,

Normally the target-runner evaluates a parameter configuration of your algorithm on a particular "problem instance". Each problem instance may be a travelling salesman problem instance or a numerical benchmark function or a particular dataset or...

If in your context, each instance is an independent file, you can put the instances in ./Instances and irace will use the name and path to the files as the "instance" that irace passes to target-runner.
Otherwise, you can describe what an instance is in the file given as "trainInstancesFile" in scenario.txt, one per line, and this is what irace will pass to target-runner.

If you have both "trainInstancesDir" (which by default is "./Instances") and "trainInstancesFile" set, then irace will take one line from the file given by "trainInstancesFile" and paste it together with the value of "trainInstancesDir", so you may end up with something like "./Instances/line 1".

You can definitely leave the "./Instances" folder empty if you use "trainInstancesFile" to specify the instances, but in that case it will be better to set trainInstancesDir="" in scenario.txt so irace will not use the default value of "./Instances/".

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: target-runner vs instances
messages.body_plain:
Yes, irace does not try to open or read the instances. It simply selects one and gives the name to the target-runner. It is the responsibility of the target-runner to know what to do with it.

You can have a trainInstancesFile="instances.txt" that contains lines like:
--scenario 1 --type A
--scenario 1 --type B
--scenario 2 --type A
...

and irace will select one of the lines of that file and pass it to the target-runner as the "instance":

/path/to/execdir/target-runner .... --scenario 2 --type A ....

The target-runner, which is always application-specific, then needs to know what to do with it.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: target-runner vs instances
messages.body_plain:
On Monday, 20 June 2022 at 18:07:02 UTC+2 ignacio....@gmail.com wrote:
> Thank you Manuel.
> Now is all clear.
> Just curious, Is it a way to avoid passing the Instance as argument?

How would the target-runner know which instance/dataset/simulation scenario your algorithm/software/configuration should be evaluated on? If your scenario does not actually have "instances" or only has 1 instance, then you can add a single line "dummy" in instances.txt and make your target-runner ignore that. But if there are no "instances" in your case, perhaps  irace is not the best tool for your use case.

> Also, I ran into a new problem. When calling the target-runner exe from the CMD exactly as R does, the exe return the objective function to be minimized, but when running iRace I get an error:
>
> Excepción no controlada: System.IO.FileLoadException: No se puede cargar el archivo o ensamblado 'System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' ni una de sus dependencias. La definición del manifiesto del ensamblado no coincide con la referencia al ensamblado. (Excepción de HRESULT: 0x80131040)
>
> Any insight on why this could be happening when the target-runner is being called from R?

This is an error from your operating system or from your target-runner, not from irace. Are you sure 100% irace is calling the target-runner exe exactly as you do from CMD? You can run irace with debugLevel=3 and see every call that irace makes.

If you run irace from CMD, you can also do "irace --check" to do a quick check that prints exactly what irace is doing. If you run irace from Rstudio, you can do:

library(irace)
irace.cmdline("--check")

Maybe some of the advice in the troubleshooting section (Appendix B) of the user-guide would be useful: https://mlopez-ibanez.github.io/irace/irace-package.pdf

To call the target-runner, irace uses the function "system2" from R: https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/system2.html
If you can run the command with system2 from R, then irace should work!

For better or worse, irace is quite good at finding hard-to-reproduce bugs in the programs that it is tuning.

If you find the solution to the problem and you think the solution may help others, please describe it in this forum.

Best,

Manuel.
